1. Use OmniRec as the experiment orchestration framework, accessing LensKit algorithms through OmniRec's LensKit wrapper interface (no direct low-level LensKit API calls).
2. Load three datasets via `RecSysDataSet.use_dataloader()` using the registered names: `DataSet.MovieLens100K`, `DataSet.Amazon2014VideoGames`, `DataSet.HetrecLastFM`.

3. Preprocess all three datasets with a `Pipe()` pipeline containing: (a) `MakeImplicit(4)` applied to MovieLens100K and Amazon2014VideoGames to convert ratings > 3 to implicit feedback (do NOT apply MakeImplicit to HetrecLastFM as it is already implicit), (b) `CorePruning(5)` for 5-core filtering on all three datasets, (c) `UserHoldout(validation_size=0.0, test_size=0.2)` for user-based 80/20 train/test split (validation set will be empty).
4. Define exactly 5 random seeds [42, 123, 456, 789, 1111] and call `set_random_state(seed)` before each repetition to control data splitting reproducibility.

5. Add three algorithms to an `ExperimentPlan` via `plan.add_algorithm()` using identifiers `LensKit.PopScorer`, `LensKit.ItemKNNScorer`, and `LensKit.ImplicitMFScorer`, each with default hyperparameters and `feedback='implicit'`.
6. Configure evaluation with `Evaluator(NDCG([1, 5, 10]), Precision([1, 5, 10]))` using ranking metrics from `omnirec.metrics.ranking`.
7. Execute all experiments (3 datasets × 5 seeds × 3 algorithms = 45 runs) and collect results.
8. Aggregate metrics across the 5 seeds and report mean and standard deviation of nDCG@k and Precision@k (k=1,5,10) for each algorithm-dataset combination.
